questions.q: Why does the retry loop only retry on a 5xx status code or a thrown exception, and not on a 4xx status code?
options: A 4xx means the request itself is wrong; retrying it just repeats the same failure instead of fixing a transient problem
4xx codes are actually more likely to succeed on retry than 5xx codes
RESTMessageV2 cannot return a 4xx status
Retrying on any status code always risks creating a duplicate record
questions.explain: 5xx and network exceptions are transient; 4xx means the request itself needs to change, which a retry can't fix.

questions.q: Looking at `existing.addQuery('u_meridian_employee_id', employee.employeeId); existing.query(); if (existing.next()) { ... return existing.getUniqueValue(); }`, what does this code protect against?
options: Network timeouts while calling Meridian HR
Expired OAuth tokens
Malformed JSON in the response body
Creating a second, duplicate sys_user if the same employee notification arrives more than once
questions.explain: This is the idempotency check — it looks for an existing record by the external ID before ever inserting a new one.

questions.q: Why does the retry delay double after each failed attempt instead of staying fixed?
options: Doubling the delay is called exponential backoff, and avoids hammering a struggling system with the same request on a fixed, aggressive interval
A fixed delay is actually illegal in ServiceNow script
Doubling the delay makes the REST Message authenticate faster
It has no real effect on the integration's behavior
questions.explain: Exponential backoff gives a struggling system increasing room to recover, instead of retrying at the same aggressive pace each time.

questions.q: In this lesson's logging approach, when is gs.error() used instead of gs.info()?
options: Every single time a retry happens, including the first one
Only when retries are fully exhausted or a response can't be parsed — cases a real on-call engineer actually needs to see
Never — gs.error() is not used anywhere in this integration
Only when the sys_user record already exists and creation is skipped
questions.explain: gs.info() covers normal operation, including retries and skipped duplicates; gs.error() is reserved for genuine failures.

questions.q: In the processNewHire orchestrator, what happens if pullEmployeeFromMeridian returns null after exhausting all retries?
options: The method logs an error and returns, without ever calling createPendingUser or createOnboardingTasks
It creates a sys_user record with blank fields anyway
It automatically retries one more time, with no limit
It silently ignores the failure and proceeds to create onboarding tasks
questions.explain: The orchestrator checks for a missing employee record and bails out before any downstream record creation runs.
